hints: Focus on what must happen to make $\text{Cl}_2$ from $\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{I}_2$ from $\text{I}^-$, think loss or gain of electrons.
Notice that iodide forms $\text{I}_2$ but chloride stays as $\text{HCl}$, so only one of these halide ions is actually oxidised by the acid.
Connect this to the role of concentrated sulfuric acid and the trend in how easily halide ions lose electrons down Group 17.
walkthrough:
**Spot the acid-base reaction first**

Both salts first react as an acid-base reaction to make the hydrogen halide.

$$\text{NaX(s) + H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(l)} \rightarrow \text{NaHSO}_4\text{(s) + HX(g)}$$
This gives $\text{HCl}$ from $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{HI}$ from $\text{NaI}$.

**Spot the second redox reaction**

Forming $\text{Cl}_2$ from $\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{I}_2$ from $\text{I}^-$ both need oxidation, loss of electrons.

$$\text{2X}^- \rightarrow \text{X}_2 + 2e^-$$
We see $\text{I}_2$ is formed, so $\text{I}^-$ is oxidised. $\text{Cl}_2$ is not formed, so $\text{Cl}^-$ is not oxidised.

**Identify the role of sulfuric acid**

If iodide is oxidised, something else must be reduced. That is concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, which is reduced to $\text{SO}_2$, S or $\text{H}_2\text{S}$. So sulfuric acid acts as an oxidising agent here.

**Explain the difference with ease of oxidation**

Iodide ions are larger with electrons further from the nucleus, so they lose electrons more easily than chloride ions. That is why sulfuric acid is strong enough to oxidise $\text{I}^-$ to $\text{I}_2$ but not $\text{Cl}^-$ to $\text{Cl}_2$.

options.A: Sulfuric acid is correctly called an oxidising agent, but chloride is not more easily oxidised. In fact $\text{Cl}_2$ is not formed, proving $\text{Cl}^-$ resists oxidation here.
options.B: Concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ acts as an oxidising agent. Iodide is more easily oxidised than chloride, so $\text{I}^-$ is oxidised to $\text{I}_2$ while $\text{Cl}^-$ stays as $\text{HCl}$.
options.C: Sulfuric acid is not acting as a reducing agent here, it gains electrons and is reduced. Also forming $\text{Cl}_2$ would be oxidation, not reduction, of chloride.
options.D: Sulfuric acid is not a reducing agent in this reaction, and forming $\text{I}_2$ from $\text{I}^-$ is oxidation (loss of electrons), not reduction.
